title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
body: An open standard for AI agents to safely access external tools and data. MCP enables Claude and other AI models to call specialized server implementations (MCPs) through a standardized protocol, similar to how web browsers use HTTP.

title: MCP Server
body: A program that implements the MCP protocol and exposes capabilities (tools, resources, prompts) to AI agents. Examples: rope-mcp (code refactoring), vscode-workspace-mcp (file operations), anthropic/filesystem-mcp (file system access).

title: MCP Client
body: The AI agent or application that connects to MCP servers and uses their capabilities. Example: Claude Code uses rope-mcp and vscode-workspace-mcp for code refactoring and file operations.

title: MCP Tool
body: A callable function exposed by an MCP server. Tools are actions the AI can perform: examples include 'extract_method' (rope-mcp), 'search_files' (vscode-mcp), 'read_file' (filesystem-mcp). Tools have inputs, outputs, and descriptions.

title: MCP Resource
body: A data artifact exposed by an MCP server (not a function). Resources are read-only and include metadata like URIs and MIME types. Example: a vector database index, a configuration file, or documentation accessible to the AI.

title: MCP Prompt
body: Reusable prompt templates exposed by an MCP server. Prompts can include dynamic arguments and are used to guide AI behavior for domain-specific tasks. Example: a code review prompt template with arguments for language and style guide.

title: Rope (rope-mcp)
body: An MCP server for Python code refactoring. Provides tools like 'extract_method', 'rename', 'move', 'inline', and 'change_signature'. Built on the rope library, it enables safe automated refactoring of Python code.

title: VSCode Workspace MCP (vscode-workspace-mcp)
body: An MCP server for file and workspace operations. Provides tools like 'read_file', 'write_file', 'list_directory', 'search_in_files', and 'get_file_info'. Enables AI agents to safely navigate and modify file systems.

title: MCP Coordinator
body: A component that routes tasks to appropriate MCP servers based on task type and available capabilities. Decides which MCP to use for a given task, handles fallback strategies when MCPs are unavailable, and logs usage telemetry.

title: MCP Registry
body: A registry that tracks available MCP servers, their capabilities, health status, and metadata. Used by MCPCoordinator to discover which MCP to route a task to based on task type or required capability.

title: MCP Capability
body: A specific operation or feature that an MCP server can perform. Examples: 'extract_method' (rope-mcp capability), 'read_file' (workspace-mcp capability). MCPCoordinator uses capabilities to match tasks to appropriate servers.

title: Fallback Strategy
body: A plan for handling tasks when the preferred MCP is unavailable. Strategies: 'claude' (use Claude's native capabilities), 'local_tools' (use CLI tools like grep/find), 'skip' (safely abort the task). MCPCoordinator selects strategy based on task type.

title: MCP Audit Trail
body: An append-only log (JSONL format) that records every MCP invocation: timestamp, task type, MCP name, agent persona, success/failure, and fallback strategy used. Used for compliance, debugging, and understanding agent behavior.

title: Agent Persona
body: A predefined role for an AI agent with specific authorization levels and task restrictions. Examples: ORCHESTRATOR (L1, can modify infrastructure), FEATURE_BUILDER (L2, can build features), COMPLIANCE_FIXER (L3, can only fix violations). Personas enforce governance.

title: MCP Transport
body: The communication mechanism between MCP client and server. MCP supports stdio (standard input/output), HTTP, and WebSocket transports. Enables flexible deployment: local processes, remote services, or embedded servers.

title: MCP Type/Category
body: Classification of MCP servers by domain: REFACTORING (code transformation), WORKSPACE (file operations), ANALYSIS (code inspection), INTEGRATION (third-party APIs), DATA (databases), CUSTOM (user-defined). Used to organize and discover MCPs.
